Facebook without the algorithm

A free browser extension that opens Facebook on the Feeds view: friends, groups and pages, most recent first. No suggested posts, no Reels tab.

What it changes on Facebook

  • Opens the Feeds view instead of Home, so facebook.com shows your friends, groups and pages in the order they posted.
  • Hides the Reels tab.

Every change is a checkbox in the popup, on its own, so you keep only the ones you want. Nothing else about Facebook changes: search, profiles, messages and posting work exactly as before.

How do I see Facebook posts in chronological order?

Facebook keeps a chronological view called Feeds, buried in the left-hand menu, and always brings you back to the algorithmic Home feed on the next visit. With the extension on, facebook.com opens on Feeds instead, every time.

What is the Facebook Feeds view?

It is Facebook’s own most-recent-first feed of your friends, groups and pages, with tabs to see each on its own. No suggested posts, no “people you may know”.

How do I hide Reels on Facebook?

A checkbox in the popup hides the Reels tab. Like every option, it works on its own if that is the only change you want.

Will Marketplace, groups and Messenger still work?

Yes. Only the feed you land on changes. Marketplace, groups, events, Messenger, notifications and posting are exactly as before, and turning the extension off puts everything back.
